items.name: Malabar spinach (poi)
items.prabhava: Upodika is the classical moistening green — cooling, gently laxative, kind to pitta where most greens are rough; the mucilage is its medicine.
items.preparation: Cook briefly — the leaves collapse fast and the mucilage thickens the dish; a summer green for hot constitutions.

items.name: Radish greens
items.prabhava: The tops most cooks discard — classical texts treat tender mulaka greens as wholesome where the mature root is heavy; peppery kapha-scrapers.
combinations: cooked with the roots in dal
viruddha: with milk (mulaka rule extends to the greens)
items.preparation: Use young tender tops; chop fine and cook with a little besan or dal to bind their bite.

items.name: Lettuce (leaf/iceberg)
contraindications: vata excess (cold raw salads as whole meals, especially at night)
items.preparation: Best at midday with a generous oil dressing; iceberg is mostly water — leaf and butterhead varieties carry more substance.
provenance: Modern usage; see dravya.romaine-lettuce for the sturdier varietal

items.name: Spring garlic greens
items.prabhava: Winter's young garlic shoots — rasona's warmth in a gentler, greener form; the seasonal signature of undhiyu and winter chutneys.
items.preparation: Chop whole stalks like spring onion; brief cooking keeps the fresh heat — a short winter-window ingredient.

items.name: Haak (Kashmiri collard)
items.prabhava: Kashmir's daily whole-leaf greens, simmered in water and mustard oil with nothing to hide behind — simplicity as the recipe.
combinations: haak with rice (the everyday Kashmiri plate)
simmered whole with mustard oil, water, and a pinch of hing
contraindications: thyroid conditions (crucifer, large raw amounts — cooked is fine)
items.preparation: Whole leaves simmered briefly in seasoned water-oil till just tender; overcooking is the only way to ruin it.

items.name: Agathi leaf
items.prabhava: Strongly bitter ritual green of Tamil tradition — eaten on dvadashi days to cleanse; classical agastya is respected and dosed with care.
combinations: agathi keerai poriyal with coconut and ghee (the traditional buffer)
contraindications: occasional-use green, not a daily staple
items.preparation: Cook well with coconut and ghee; tradition assigns it specific days — a periodic cleanser, not an everyday saag.

items.name: Dwarf copperleaf (ponnanganni)
items.prabhava: The 'golden eye' green of Tamil tradition — matsyakshi is classically linked with eye nourishment and cooling clarity.
items.preparation: Quick-cook with coconut like any keerai; tradition gives it a weekly place for eyes and skin.

items.name: Black nightshade greens
items.prabhava: Kakamachi is the classical ulcer-soothing green — Tamil households cook it for mouth ulcers and gut heat; a food-medicine of the old lists.
combinations: vathal (sun-dried berries) fried in ghee for curd rice
contraindications: only ripe berries and cooked leaves — unripe green berries carry solanine
items.preparation: Cook leaves like keerai; the sun-dried berry (vathal) fried in ghee is the famous curd-rice companion.
items.reviewNote: Classical kakamachi is described as tridoshic; hint and sources vary on virya. Safety note on unripe berries is firm.

items.name: Pumpkin tendrils and leaves
items.preparation: Strip the fibrous strings from stems, cook tips and young leaves briefly — the whole vine feeds, not just the fruit.

items.name: Chakvad greens (cassia tora)
items.prabhava: Monsoon wild green of central India — chakramarda is the classical skin-tradition plant; young leaves are cooked as a seasonal cleanser.
combinations: takla bhaji with garlic and chili (Maharashtrian monsoon dish)
items.preparation: Pick young monsoon leaves, boil-discard the first water, then cook with garlic — the traditional detox bhaji protocol.

items.name: Dry dates (chhuara)
items.prabhava: The hard sun-dried date — kharjura concentrated; boiled soft in milk it becomes the classical winter strength drink of North Indian homes.
combinations: boiled in milk until soft (chhuara doodh)
items.preparation: Never eat dry-hard; soak overnight or simmer in milk 10 minutes until the flesh yields. Remove the stone before serving.
provenance: Kharjura lineage; North Indian winter tradition
items.reviewNote: Soft fresh dates exist as dravya.dates (batch 05); this is the distinct dried-hard chhuara form. Predraft soft-dates skipped as duplicate.

items.name: Dried water chestnut
items.prabhava: Sun-dried singhara kernels — ground into the fasting flour, or soaked and cooked as a cooling, astringent strengthener.
items.preparation: Soak before cooking whole, or use the flour; the fresh nut's coolness survives drying with added heaviness.

items.name: Dried cranberry
combinations: in warm porridges and grain salads
soaked in warm water for vata
items.preparation: Commercial dried cranberries are candied — treat as a sweet-sour accent, not a fruit serving.

items.name: Dried lotus seed (kamal gatta)
items.prabhava: True lotus (Nelumbo) seed — sacred, astringent-sweet and grounding; distinct from makhana (Euryale fox nut) despite market confusion.
contraindications: remove the bitter green germ before cooking
items.preparation: Soak well, split and remove the bitter embryo, then simmer — the seed turns chestnut-soft.
items.reviewNote: Distinct from dravya.lotus-seed (makhana, batch 07) — different species; both traditional.

items.name: Panchmeva (five dry fruits)
items.prabhava: The ritual five-dry-fruit blend — almond, raisin, dried date, cashew/walnut and dried coconut (or makhana); prasada that doubles as a classical ojas formula.
items.preparation: Small handful portions; soaking or milk-simmering converts a heavy mix into a workable winter builder. Ensure any date or prune component is stoned before serving.

items.name: White sesame seed
items.prabhava: The hulled, pale tila of sweets and tahini — gentler than black sesame, same warming unctuous nature.
items.preparation: Roast until pale gold and fragrant; grind or chew well — whole seeds pass through.
items.reviewNote: Generic sesame exists as dravya.sesame-seed (batch 07); white and black varietals kept for classical distinction (krishna tila ranked highest).

items.name: Black sesame seed
items.prabhava: Krishna tila is the classical best of sesame — deepest building for bones, hair and vata; the seed of winter solstice rituals and ancestral offerings.
items.preparation: Roast gently — black seeds hide scorching; grind fresh for maximum virtue. Classical texts rank this the supreme tila.

items.name: Sweet basil seed (sabja)
items.prabhava: The original falooda seed — swells into cooling gel like chia but faster; the traditional summer heat-and-acidity soother of sherbet stalls.
combinations: soaked into falooda, rose milk and sherbets
contraindications: always pre-soak (swelling seeds; never dry by the spoon)
items.preparation: Soak 15 minutes until each seed wears its gel halo; stir into any cool drink.

items.name: Muskmelon seed
items.prabhava: Char magaz member — the four cooling melon-cucumber seeds of Unani-Ayurvedic summer tonics and thandai.
items.preparation: Use peeled kernels; grind into summer drinks — cooling fat and protein against the heat.

items.name: Cucumber seed (magaz)
items.prabhava: The fourth of the char magaz quartet — cucumber's coolness concentrated into a kernel; traditional urinary-heat soother.
items.preparation: Peeled kernels ground with the other magaz seeds; rarely used alone.

items.name: Garden cress seed (halim)
items.prabhava: Chandrashura is the classical postpartum and strength seed — iron-dense red kernels that swell like sabja but warm like mustard; aliv laddus rebuild new mothers.
combinations: aliv laddu with coconut and jaggery (Maharashtrian postpartum)
contraindications: pregnancy (uterine stimulant — postpartum is the tradition, pregnancy is not)
items.preparation: Soak in milk or water until gelled, then into laddus or drinks; a teaspoon carries a day's iron tradition.
